title: What is Depression
situation: A 25-year-old user suspects they may have depression but is unsure what it actually is. They want to understand the condition before deciding whether to seek help.
user_turns: I've been feeling really low for months. Someone told me I might have depression but I don't really know what that means. What is depression exactly?
So is it just feeling sad? Because I don't always feel sad — sometimes I just feel completely empty and numb.
How do I know if what I'm experiencing is depression or just a rough patch? Is there a difference?
What are the treatment options? I'm nervous about medication.

title: Understanding Anxiety Disorders
situation: A 22-year-old university student experiences panic attacks and wants to understand what is happening to their body and whether it is dangerous.
user_turns: I keep having these episodes where my heart races, I can't breathe, and I feel like I'm dying. What is happening to me?
Someone said it might be a panic attack. What causes those? Why does my body do that?
Is it dangerous? I'm scared that one day my heart will actually give out during one of these episodes.
What's the difference between a panic attack and a heart attack? How do I know which one it is?

title: PTSD Explanation
situation: A 34-year-old who experienced a traumatic event two years ago is still having flashbacks and nightmares. They want to understand why this is still happening.
user_turns: I went through something traumatic two years ago and I still have nightmares and flashbacks. I thought I'd be over it by now. What's wrong with me?
What is PTSD exactly? I always thought it was something only soldiers got.
Why does my brain keep replaying the event even when I don't want it to? It feels like I have no control.
What treatments actually work for PTSD? I've heard about different therapies but I don't know which one to try.

title: How CBT Works
situation: A 29-year-old has been referred to CBT therapy by their doctor but has no idea what it involves. They want to understand the process before committing.
user_turns: My doctor recommended CBT but I don't know what it is. Can you explain how it works?
So it's about changing thoughts? But what if my thoughts are accurate — what if my situation really is bad?
How long does CBT usually take? I'm worried about committing to something long-term.
What's the difference between CBT and just talking to a friend about your problems?

title: Sleep and Mental Health
situation: A 38-year-old is struggling with insomnia and wants to understand the relationship between sleep and mental health.
user_turns: I haven't been sleeping well for months. I know it's affecting my mood but I don't understand why sleep is so important for mental health.
What is sleep hygiene? My doctor mentioned it but didn't explain it properly.
I've tried going to bed earlier but I just lie there for hours. What's actually happening in my brain when I can't sleep?
Are sleeping pills safe to use long-term? I'm tempted to just take something to knock me out.

title: Difference Between Sadness and Depression
situation: A 20-year-old is confused about whether what they are experiencing is normal sadness or clinical depression, and wants to understand the distinction.
user_turns: Everyone feels sad sometimes, right? How do I know if what I'm feeling is just normal sadness or something more serious like depression?
I've been feeling low for about six weeks. Is that too long for normal sadness?
What are the signs that someone should actually seek professional help versus just waiting it out?
If I go to a doctor, what will they actually do? I'm worried they'll just put me on medication straight away.

title: Anxiety vs Stress
situation: A 27-year-old professional is unsure whether they have an anxiety disorder or are just experiencing normal work stress. They want to understand the difference.
user_turns: I'm always worried about work, money, relationships — basically everything. Is that anxiety or just normal stress? Everyone seems stressed these days.
What's the actual clinical definition of an anxiety disorder? When does worry become a disorder?
I've heard about generalised anxiety disorder. What is that exactly and how is it different from just being a worrier?
Can anxiety go away on its own or does it always need treatment?
